newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Denmark asks for flight row meeting with Estonia.
newsitem.headline: Denmark asks for flight row meeting with Estonia.

text.p: Danish Transport Minister Jan Troejborg has asked for a meeting with Estonian counterpart Kalev Kukk over a row on flying rights between Scandinavia and Estonia, the Estonian Civil Aviation Authority said on Friday.
Denmark also suggested extending the present timetable so that flights will not have to be suspended after a November 16 deadline, a spokesman for the aviation authority told Reuters.

"Today a fax arrived from the Danish minister of transport with the suggestion of holding a meeting with Estonian Minister of Transport and Communications Kalev Kukk," the spokeswoman said in a statement.

The row began after Estonia asked Scandinavian Airlines to cut its flights between Denmark and Estonia to one a day from two as Estonian Air, part-owned by Maersk, wanted to resume its flights to Copenhagen.
Estonia also refused to allow SAS to fly twice a day between Tallinn and Stockholm.
The Estonian side says three flights a day between its capital, Denmark and Sweden would too much capacity on these routes, an argument which SAS rejects.
SAS is also involved in a row between Russia and Latvia, where it owns a major stake in state airline Air Baltic.
